To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) EF binding to CaM reduces the calcium affinity of N-Ca-M, (b) the effect of EF on the calcium affinity of the N-CAM binding sites is mediated by a direct restraint on Site 2, by an indirect stabilization of Site 1 and by reducing the coupling between the two sites.

EF impairs CaM binding by a direct restraint on the calcium binding site, an indirect destabilization on a neighboring binding site, and a reduction in the cooperativity between calcium binding sites.
EF impairs the calcium binding of N-CaMD through a direct con-formational restraint on the Site 1, and an indirect destabilization Site 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of the EF-CAM interaction with calcium binding and the resulting modulation of the Ca2+ affinity of N-Ca2+.
the molecular mechanism of the interplay between the CaM binding sites, the EF binding site, and the calcium binding sites.
the role of calcium in regulating the interaction between CaM and its target, and with the role of CaM in the regulation of the calcium binding properties of its target.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EF binding to CaM reduces the affinity of the N-CAM domains for calcium by a direct and an indirect action, and by reducing cooperativity.
CaM is a flexible protein that is able to bind multiple targets, but that this ability is not a general property.
EF impairs CaM calcium affinity by a direct effect on the calcium-binding sites and an indirect effect on the CaM domains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CaM is a flexible protein which can be stabilized by EF, and that the EF-Ca ^{2+} -CaM complex is stabilized by CaM.
CaM and EF interact through a delicate balance of electrostatics and conformational changes, and that EF binding to N-CaM is favored at low calcium concentrations.

EF and calmodulin interact through multiple weak electrostatic interactions, which are sufficient to stabilize the complex, but are not strong enough to prevent the calcium-induced opening of N-Cam domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EF-CaMs complex is stabilized by a balance between electrostatic interactions between EF and CaM, and the calcium affinity of the protein.
the EF-Ca-M interaction and calcium binding are coupled.
the EF-Ca-M interaction is not a static complex, but a dynamic one that is affected by calcium binding.
